kaede.title: Two Stolen Bottles
kaede.text:
Kaede hauls you up the ladder to the roof with two bottles of wine she very obviously did not pay for. The glass is still cold and sweating from the cellar. The tiles have kept the day's warmth, chimney smoke drifts across the stars, and somewhere below a late client is singing badly on his way home.

She pulls the first cork with her teeth and drinks before she passes it over.

"We were called the Copper Foxes," she says to the rooftops. "Four of us. When the floor went in that dungeon, our leader was the first one out, and he didn't look back to count." Her tail thumps the tiles once. "I learned to check my own corners after that. Then a skinny guy in a hoodie throws himself in front of a crossbow for me, and I've known him about nine seconds."

She bumps your shoulder with hers.

"Idiot."

She doesn't move away afterward. Her tail settles lightly around your ankle.
ngpp: She stops with the cork half out and stares at the label. For a second her ears tilt as if she's heard this exact pop before, on some other roof. "Huh," she says. She shakes it off and drinks.

"Weird question, Sam. Have we sat up here before? Drinking cheaper stuff than this?" Her tail has already found your boot and hooked around the ankle, like it knows the way. She frowns at it. She doesn't move it.

She doesn't pretend it's casual this time. Her tail goes straight behind your ankle. "Don't ask me how I know you like the east chimney, Sam. I do. We've done this. I don't know how many times. Just pour."

choices.label: Stay on the roof with her
choices.res: You stay. The second bottle goes the way of the first, and the stars seem to come down a little. She tells you about the friend who didn't make it out, and you don't say anything clever. Her tail never unwinds from your ankle. Neither of you points it out, and when she finally climbs down she does it backwards, so she can keep looking at you.

choices.label: Pass the conversation back to her wine
choices.res: You ask whether the wine is any good and point at the label. {N} snorts into the neck of the bottle, and you can see her shoulders loosen as she lets you change the subject. She rates the vintage a six, then a seven, then argues with herself about it. Her tail still sneaks one lazy swish against your leg as you both climb down.

image.comp: sitting on a rooftop at night bumping shoulders with him, holding a wine bottle, fox tail swishing
image.setting: tiled rooftop over a fantasy town at night, stars, chimney smoke

kaede.title: Wrong Door
kaede.text:
You shoulder open the washroom door with a towel over your arm and your mind on the ledger, and Kaede is standing in the middle of the floor with one foot up on the stool.

She has a towel. It's mostly on. Steam is curling off her sun-browned skin, and the thin scar on her shoulder has gone pink from the heat. She had been humming something, and she has stopped.

Every hair on her tail stands straight out, like a bottlebrush.

For one long second the only sound is a tap dripping. You can feel all the words you know leaving your head in an orderly line. Her ears swivel toward you one at a time. You can see her deciding whether this is funny or a fight.

1.title: Share the Steam
1.text:
You push open the washroom door, and Kaede is sitting on the edge of the steaming tub with her wet hair stuck to one collarbone and a towel tucked loosely around her hips. Her ears come up. Her tail does not fluff this time.

"You forgot how to knock again." The grin is bold, but the blush under it is real. She rolls her scarred shoulder and winces. "Or did you come to be useful? I took a chair leg across the back tonight, breaking up those two dockhands, and I can't reach it."

She holds the soap out to you over her shoulder without turning around, and she waits.

choices.label: Offer to scrub the knot out of her scarred shoulder
choices.res: You take the soap and kneel behind her on the wet boards. She lets the towel drop to her waist and blows out a shaky breath. Your slick palms work down her bare shoulder blades, over the old scar, and the knot under it finally gives. She spins around in the steam, grabs your collar and pulls your mouth onto hers.
choices.fallbackRes: You work the knot out of her shoulder with your thumbs, slow and steady, until the muscle goes soft under the soap. Her tail thumps against the wet wood twice and then goes still. She leans back against your chest, eyes shut, and stays there with her wet hair on your shirt. Neither of you says anything. It's enough.

choices.label: Hand her a fresh towel and give her space
choices.res: You hand her a fresh towel and look at the wall. "Gentleman tonight, huh?" she says. She takes it, and you hear her rubbing her hair dry behind you. When you glance back, her grin is crooked and pleased, and her tail has curled around your wrist. It stays there a long, lingering second before she lets go.

3.title: No Towel Needed
3.text:
The washroom is thick with steam when you step inside, and Kaede doesn't reach for the towel on the stool.

She's sitting waist-deep in the tub with her arms along the rim, water running off her bare tits, copper hair dark and loose down her back. She looks you over slowly, the way she looks over a room she's about to clear. Then she hooks one wet ankle behind your calf and pulls.

"Lock the bolt, Sam." Her tail slaps the water. "Unless you only came in here to stare. I don't mind that either, but I had plans."

choices.label: Lock the door and get into the tub with her
choices.res: You lock the bolt, kick your boots off and get in with your clothes half on. Water slops over the rim. Kaede doesn't wait for you to settle. She climbs over your lap with a wicked grin, her wet tits against your shirt and her hands already at your belt. Her tail slaps the water behind her, and she kisses you hard.

choices.label: Tease her and wash her back first
choices.res: You kneel beside the tub and rub lather across her shoulders, down her back, then around the front over her tits. She groans. She tries to keep the grin going and doesn't manage it. When she twists around, the water runs off her arms, and she drags your wet shirt toward the tub with both fists, still laughing at you.

choices.label: Apologize and bolt
choices.res: You back out and apologize to the door. Kaede laughs for ten minutes. She does it through the wood and loudly enough that the whole corridor learns what happened. At dinner she toasts you with a spoon, and every time you look up she is watching you with her ears pricked and her tail swinging, very pleased with herself.

choices.label: Compliment her
choices.res: You tell her she looks good, and you mean it. She grins, and her tail slowly settles. She doesn't hold the towel very hard. "Smooth, Sam. Real smooth." She takes her time looking you over in return, from boots to hair, and her voice drops when she says it. The warmth in it outlasts the steam.

else.res: "GET OUT." The towel hits you square in the face. It's still warm and smells of her soap. The door slams behind you hard enough to rattle the hinges, and you hear her swear on the other side, then a thump that might be the stool. You'll be apologizing for this one for a few days.

choices.label: Stand there like an idiot
choices.res: You stand there and say nothing at all. "Take a picture, it lasts longer," she says. You have no idea how she knows that phrase, but she is smirking when she says it. Her tail is fluffed with pride, not panic. She lets you look a few seconds longer before she throws the soap at your head.

image.comp: frozen mid-towel in a washroom doorway, every hair on her fox tail standing straight up, wide-eyed

kaede.title: Tail Says Otherwise
kaede.text:
Kaede turns up at your door after closing with a bandaged hand and a grin that's a little too bright. She says she got hurt sparring. "For fun," she adds, before you've asked.

The linen is a mess. She has plainly tied it one-handed with her teeth. Underneath, the knuckles are split and puffy, and she smells of liniment and sawdust. You've already heard from the bar that a man said something about the new girl, and that Kaede walked him out through the yard.

She sits on the edge of your bed while you unwind it and start again. You aren't good at this. She watches your hands anyway, as if nobody has ever done it for her, and it's likely nobody has.

Her tail keeps brushing your arm, back and forth, warm and soft. Neither of you mentions it. She doesn't tell you what the man said, and you find you don't need her to.

choices.label: Finish the bandage and pull her close
choices.res: You tie off the linen, and Kaede catches your collar with her good hand before you can sit back. She tips over onto the mattress and pulls you down with her, her tail tight around your waist and her bandaged fist braced beside your head. She is grinning and out of breath, and she kisses you before you can ask if her hand hurts.

choices.label: Finish the bandage slowly
choices.res: You take your time over the knot. She lets you, with her eyes on your hands instead of the wall. When it's done you smooth the edge flat with your thumb, and she turns her hand over and looks at it as if it belongs to someone else. Her tail stops pretending to be an accident. It wraps around your wrist and stays.

choices.label: Tie it off and tease her about sparring
choices.res: "For fun," you repeat, deadpan, and pull the knot tight. {N} flicks your ear for it. Then she laughs, low and a little rough, and she doesn't get up. She sits on the edge of your bed a minute longer than she needs to and bumps her knee against yours. Her tail slides across your forearm once, back and forth.

image.comp: sitting on a kitchen table while he bandages her hand, grinning, fox tail brushing his arm
image.setting: inn kitchen at night, a first-aid kit

kaede.title: The Old Party
kaede.text:
Kaede's old party leader turns up at the bar on a wet night in dungeon-stained leathers, with the smell of rain and old smoke coming in behind him. He's handsome in a worn way, and he smiles like a man who has always been forgiven.

He has a new contract. It's a deep delve with a real payout, and there's a place in it for a scout who knows how he works. He says the Foxes should never have broken up, and he doesn't say whose fault that was.

The common room goes quiet. Somebody sets a mug down very carefully.

Kaede doesn't look at him. She's behind the bar with a rag in her fist, and she looks at you. Her ears are pinned flat. Her fingers start drumming on the counter, the way they do when she's counting something.

She isn't asking your permission. She has decided to find out what you'll say.
ngpp: The scarred adventurer steps up to the bar, and Kaede gives him an odd, impatient look. It's as if she has already told this man no, and was hoping he wouldn't make her do it twice.

"Why does it feel like he always walks in wearing the same muddy boots?" she mutters, out of the side of her mouth. Her ears are pinned. She's waiting for you to say the word, and she knows what it will be.

She doesn't let the captain finish his pitch. She slides along the bar until her shoulder is against your elbow. "Same answer as always, Sam. I've given it before. Just say the word, and I'll give it again."

choices.label: "Go, if it's what you want."
choices.res: "Go, if it's what you want," you say. You mean it, and it costs you. Kaede's ears drop. She stays. Later she mutters into her cup, "You weren't supposed to make it easy." She doesn't look at you while she says it. But she sits close the rest of the night, hip to hip, and her tail stays on your side of the bench.

choices.label: "Stay. Please."
choices.res: "Stay. Please." She turns the leader down without looking at him, and he leaves with his ears burning and his contract folded back into his coat. The common room breathes out. Under the bar her tail slaps your leg twice, hard, happy. She wipes down the same patch of counter for a full minute so nobody will see her face.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.res: You say nothing. The old captain waits, and so does the room, and you let it run out. Kaede puts the rag down and leaves for two days without a word. When she comes back she doesn't mention it, and neither do you. It sits between you for a while, like a bill nobody wants to read, and her tail stays down.

image.comp: standing at a bar between him and a rugged adventurer in armor, arms crossed, looking at him and waiting
image.setting: busy tavern bar, adventurers at tables

kaede.title: Rooftops
kaede.text:
Kaede decides you need to learn the rooftops. Her reasoning is that a man who owns a house in Hollowmere should know how to leave it quickly.

She goes first, slate to slate in the moonlight, as though gravity were only a suggestion. She doesn't make a sound. Her tail streams out behind her for balance, and she looks back at every gap to make sure you're watching how it's done.

You are in a grey hoodie and a borrowed cloak, and you are very bad at this. You windmill across a gap a child could step over. You cling to a chimney. You apologize to a pigeon.

Kaede crouches on the ridge above you with her hands on her knees, wheezing with laughter.

"Again," she manages. "Do the pigeon again. No, don't. Jump. I'll catch you if it goes wrong. I'm serious, Sam. I will always catch you."

2.text:
Kaede takes you back up onto the rooftops, and tonight she doesn't leave you stranded at the chimney. She stays within arm's reach. Every time you wobble she's already there, with a hand flat on your chest or her tail pressed across the small of your back, and she's slow to take either one away.

You make three jumps in a row without dying. She whoops, and a shutter bangs open down the street.

Afterward you sit against a dormer that's still warm from the sun, under both moons. She's breathing hard and grinning, with her thigh against yours. She keeps glancing at your mouth and then at the skylight of the empty loft beside you, as if she's working out a route.

choices.label: Keep trying
choices.res: You keep trying. You slip, scrape both palms and hit a gutter with your knee. Near midnight you finally clear a gap cleanly. Kaede cheers loud enough to wake the whole street, and a shutter bangs open below you both. Neither of you cares. She hauls you in by the hood and rubs your hair flat, grinning, and says that is two out of fifty.

choices.label: Fake a sprained ankle so she carries you
choices.res: You grab your ankle and groan. She sees through it at once, and her ears twitch with delight. She carries you anyway, the whole way home, over her shoulder like a sack of flour, grumbling that you weigh nothing. You can feel her laughing through her ribs. She doesn't put you down until the kitchen door, and then she does it slowly.

choices.label: Duck through the attic skylight together into the empty loft
choices.res: Kaede drops through the skylight onto a pile of spare blankets and looks up at you with a grin. Then she hooks a finger into your collar and tugs you in after her. You land half on top of her. Dust floats in the moonlight. She pulls your hoodie up over your head and kisses you, breathing hard, her tail already around your thigh.

image.comp: leaping across rooftops at night, laughing back at the man clinging to a chimney
image.setting: moonlit rooftops of a fantasy town

kaede.title: Copper Fox, Kept
kaede.text:
After closing, Kaede corners you in the kitchen. The stove is ticking as it cools and one lamp is burning low. She has a stack of bar receipts in her hand, the ones with the tally on the backs, and she drops them on the table between you.

She drums her fingers on them. She stops, and starts again.

"I'm bad at this, so I'll just say it." Her ears are red to the tips. "I kept the ledger so I'd know when I was allowed to leave. I stopped adding it up a while ago. I'm not going anywhere, Sam. Not for the money, and not because I owe you. For you."

Her tail won't stop wagging, and she glares at it.

Then she takes your hand, pulls you toward the stairs, and doesn't let go of it until the bedroom door is shut behind you both.
ngpp: She laughs as she pulls you toward the stairs, breathless and a little puzzled. It feels like she's waited through more than one quiet kitchen to finally get to lock this door, and she can't say why.
"Don't laugh, Sam. I swear I've stood by this exact stove blushing my tail off before." Her fingers squeeze yours tight. She looks at the stove, then at you, as if one of them should explain it.
"Forget whatever got scrubbed off the calendar," she whispers, against your throat. "I know it happened. Every time, it ends with me backing you into this room. I'm done pretending I don't remember."
kaede.goLead: Kaede pushes the bedroom door shut with her heel and wraps both arms straight around your neck, her copper tail tangling behind your thighs as she kisses you fiercely.

choices.label: Say yes
Not yet
choices.res: {N} nods too fast. "I can wait. Don't make it too long." Her tail droops, then perks up again, stubborn. She squares the stack of receipts and tucks it under her arm. At the door she points at you, ears still red. "Soon, Sam." She sounds almost angry about it.
